newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai's tax income up 26.9 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai's tax income up 26.9 pct in 1996.

text.p: Shanghai produced 28.85 billion yuan in tax revenues for its own use in 1996, up 26.9 percent from the previous year, a city official said on Thursday.
The city took in a total of 55.55 billion yuan in tax revenue in 1996, with the rest being passed on to the central government in Beijing, the official said.

Meanwhile, the Business News said on Thursday the growth of tax revenue for Shanghai's own use will slow in the next few years after three years of sharp rises because of tax policy adjustments and the poor condition of state firms in the city.

The official newspaper said that from this month, the central government had begun taking 80 percent of the stamp tax on stock and state debt trading, up from 50 percent in the past, leaving less for the local government.
It said that adjustments to export tax rebates would also have an impact on the city's income.
